The new rules should foster the inherent advantage of motor carriage with respect to urban area operations. As noted in the Interim Report, motor carriage is characterized by a high degree of geographic and functional flexibility. In general, motor vehicles can move on short notice to a shipper location, wherever it may be, and can handle a wide range of traffic. Within urban areas, there has been an accelerating level of economic activity on the suburban periphery, and the alignment of shipper locations is evolving. local carriage exemption of section 203(b)(8) enables motor carriers to utilize their flexibility and to respond quickly to the changing needs of urban area shippers. Expansion of commercial zones will extend this versatility of motor carrier service to shippers who have migrated to points beyond present zone limits and to those shippers located in suburban industrial parks. Larger terminal and service area limits will permit many carriers to recapture traffic that was lost due to a shift in shipper location from inside to outside existing zone limits. These larger limits will frequently enable carriers to continue to render service to migrating shippers without going through the expense and delay of the certification process or resorting to the purchase of operating rights.
